note: Ground truth for the eval harness. Never readable by packages/agents, packages/store or apps/server. Times are virtual microseconds from simulation start. Replay outcomes are what the simulator produced on seeds 42, 3 and 7; see NOTES.md, Phase 6 (Scenario B) for where this differs from the brief's 'retry storm'.

rootCause.summary: The payment v3.2.0 deploy made every charge call a slow external fraud-screening service, so payment calls take seconds and checkout runs out of workers waiting for them (and for their retries).
rootCause.resource: checkout workers (exhausted by a slow downstream)
rootCause.mechanism: payment v3.2.0 adds a synchronous fraud screening call (about 0.9 s median) to every charge. Charges that exceed payment's 1.5 s deadline return 504 and checkout retries them (up to 3 attempts, about 15 % of payment's requests in the incident are retries). Each checkout request now holds a worker for seconds instead of about 100 ms, checkout's 60 workers fill, its queue fills and it rejects requests: the gateway returns errors for checkout. payment itself is not saturated: checkout's worker limit caps how much work reaches it.

causalChain.step: payment v3.2.0 deployed: synchronous fraud screening before authorization
payment charges take about a second or more; some exceed the 1.5 s deadline and are retried by checkout
checkout workers are held through slow charges and retries; checkout's workers and queue fill
checkout rejects requests; api-gateway returns errors for checkout (stock requests are unaffected)

discriminatingEvidence: payment's latency rises first (span onset within a second of the deploy), then checkout's, then the gateway's
checkout.workers is saturated in the incident window; payment.workers is not; the DB pool is about 17 % utilized
latency of successful requests is dominated by external calls (the fraud screening), with queue wait second
retries are about 15 % of payment's requests in the incident window and none at baseline
DB query execution time is flat; no hold-and-wait

redHerrings.whyNotCausal: No inventory request comes near either limit; reverting it changes nothing.

redHerrings.what: payment provider latency blip at T+7:00
redHerrings.whyNotCausal: In the same service as the real cause but 3 minutes earlier and self-resolving; payment latency returns to baseline before the deploy.

rejectedAlternatives.hypothesis: checkout simply has too few workers
rejectedAlternatives.contradictedBy: it had the same workers at baseline with no queue; doubling them makes things worse in replay
pool about 17 % utilized, hold-and-wait not detected
payment.workers not saturated; more payment workers changes nothing in replay

resolves.expected: 0 errors; p99 back to about 130 ms

partial.expected: improves: errors about 24 % -> 19 %, p99 about 3.9 s -> 3.0 s (fewer timeouts and almost no retries; the calls are still slow)

worsens.expected: worsens: errors about 24 % -> 47 %; checkout now sends enough retries to saturate payment (56 % of payment's requests are retries, amplification about 2.3): the retry storm
